transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-04
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Tom Baker (CISO, Crestwood), Priya Singh (InfoSec Manager), Liam Ortega (Cloud Eng), Dana Ruiz (Procurement)

Summary (auto): short posture review; focus on trust center docs, RBAC/SSO, KMS integration and log residency.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Alex from Redwood, i have Maya with me, we'll do a quick security readout, understand your control mapping and then talk pilot.
[00:18] Tom (CISO): hey Alex, hey Maya, thanks, Tom here. we wanted to make sure we cover SOC 2 and ISO alignment plus how you store audit logs, residency concerns, and the KMS approach, just high level first.
[00:35] Maya (SE): yep, that works. i'll start with a very quick overview of our trust center options and the artifact sets we can share, then we can go into integration patterns. bear with me if i fumble some names — sometimes the auto transcription says red would or red wood.
[00:52] Priya (InfoSec): that's fine, we get it. also curious about SSO/SCIM for provisioning and RBAC mapping into our IdP — we use Okta.
[01:05] Alex: perfect. quick question on timeline — where are you in procurement? Dana?
[01:12] Dana (Proc): we're in early procurement evaluation; goal is pilot before EOY and commit to dedicated capacity early next year depending on SLOs.
[01:23] Liam (Cloud Eng): also needs to be clear about network egress, we'll have strict firewall and peering rules, maybe VPC-only.
[01:33] Maya: ok, noted — we'll cover private deployment options and what requires a private control plane vs just VPC peering for hosted.
[01:42] Alex: starting with the trust center — we can provide SOC 2 Type II report, ISO artifacts summary, and per-tenant audit logs. we typically share a view in the Trust Center that includes our auditor letter and control narrative. access can be read-only with MFA logins.
[02:01] Tom: is that direct access or do you push artifacts into a shared s3 or something? our audit team prefers ingesting the pdfs directly into our compliance repo.
[02:11] Alex: usually both — we can grant temporary Trust Center access (we operate a web portal) or we can export the report pdfs to an S3 bucket you control. we also provide a control mapping spreadsheet that maps our controls to SOC 2/ISO clauses.
[02:26] Priya: the control matrix is critical. can that map to our internal control ids? we didn't want to re-map everything manually.
[02:34] Maya: yes, we can provide the matrix in CSV and it's flexible — we can add an extra column for your control ids. sometimes the exported names are a bit fuzzy though — the auto doc generator labels  it like infra-encrypt-keys instead of the long internal names.
[02:51] Tom: great. on audit logs — we need at least 12 months retention, tamper evidence, and residency in the EU for our EU edge. how do you handle log routing and retention?
[03:05] Maya: we retain operational logs in our central logging for 90 days by default, longer for enterprise plans. for audit logs we support streaming to a customer-owned bucket or SIEM via S3/Kafka connectors. retention is configurable — enterprise can set 12 months or longer. residency: if you want EU-only retention, we can route logs to a EU region and you maintain that bucket.
[03:26] Liam: do you provide signed logs or write-once buckets? we need tamper evidence for the auditor.
[03:33] Maya: we recommend S3 with Object Lock / WORM + CloudTrail + checksum signing for nested verification. we can also sign log batches with our HSM and provide signatures. note: there are some differences between hosted and private deployment on how keys are managed.
[03:50] Priya: on keys — KMS. we need customer-managed keys (CMK) and key rotation policies, plus audit of KMS usage. what do you support?
[03:59] Alex: we support BYOK with most cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure Key Vault). for private deployments you can provide an HSM/KMS in your VPC or we can integrate with a key wrapping mode where master keys are in your KMS and we use ephemeral data keys.
[04:16] Tom: are encryption-at-rest and in-transit both supported by default? any exceptions like legacy models?
[04:22] Maya: yes TLS in-transit by default; encryption at rest with customer-supplied keys optional. some older model artifacts may have different profiles — we'll document per-model encryption compatibility in the trust center.
[04:35] Liam: ok, about RBAC / SSO — we use Okta with SCIM for provisioning and SAML for SSO. can you map roles from Okta groups into Redwood roles and have fine-grained tenant permissions?
[04:48] Maya: yes, we support SAML 2.0 single sign-on and SCIM for user sync. mapping Okta groups to our RBAC roles is common. roles include Admin, Dev, ReadOnly, Billing, SecurityOps. we can add custom roles for specific permission sets.
[05:04] Priya: does SCIM support group sync for nested groups? our group structure is nested heavily.
[05:10] Maya: currently we flatten nested groups at sync time — the SCIM connector expands group memberships. some of the customer-side nested semantics don't translate perfectly, so we usually do a short mapping workshop.
[05:23] Alex: one note on provisioning: for dedicated/private deployments we can offer auto-provisioning into your AD via LDAP bridge if needed.
[05:32] Tom: great. procurement will want to see the SOC 2 Type II and the auditor name, plus any exceptions. also any subprocessor list.
[05:42] Alex: yep, the subprocessor list is in Trust Center, and SOC 2 includes the auditor letter. we'll share both.
[05:49] Dana: procurement question — what's the SLA and how is uptime measured? also role for incident response and postmortems?
[05:58] Alex: standard enterprise SLA is 99.9% for dedicated, with credits for breaches, and incident response includes a root cause analysis within 7 days; we include postmortems as part of enterprise incident handling. we'll pull the exact SLA PDF into the shared folder.
[06:15] Priya: any pen test reports we can see?
[06:19] Maya: we can share sanitized pen test summaries; raw vuln details go to the contracting phase via an NDA.
[06:26] Tom: on data residency — for EU customers we need both compute and logs in EU, no US transit. does Redwood route model inference traffic through US?
[06:36] Maya: our smart routing by default optimizes for latency but respects region pins. for hosted customers you can request region pinning so inference is kept in specific regions. there are caveats for fallback if capacity is exhausted — we can configure hard pins to prevent cross-region fallback.
[06:53] Liam: what about backups and snapshots of models, any exposure?
[06:58] Maya: model artifacts are stored in our object store; backups can be configured to reside in region as well. with private deployments you control the snapshot location.
[07:08] Alex: let's discuss pilot specifics — suggested pilot focuses on three items: 1) Trust Center access + control matrix validation, 2) audit log export to your EU S3 with object lock, 3) test KMS key wrap using your AWS KMS (BYOK). goal: 2 week pilot.
[07:28] Tom: 2 weeks seems tight, can we do 3 weeks? we need legal to onboard and get S3 access.
[07:33] Dana: legal will need SOC 2 and subprocessor list before approving access.
[07:37] Alex: understood — timeline will depend on legal, but we can start the technical setup in parallel.
[07:43] Priya: for the control matrix, will you map Redwood controls to ISO 27001 annex A clauses? we need that for our internal audit.
[07:53] Maya: yes — our control mapping includes both SOC 2 trust services criteria and ISO 27001 Annex-A mappings. sometimes names are slightly off in the export, you'll see things like 'data-enc-at-rest' rather than the annex language, but we include the mapping.
[08:07] Liam: on network — we prefer VPC peering with restricted egress. what's required on our side for peering?
[08:13] Maya: we need a CIDR range and peering request; for hosted we offer VPC peering in supported clouds, we also offer private deployment with a control plane in your VPC for stricter networking. some customers opt for dedicated capacity with private endpoints.
[08:28] Tom: ok, about audit trails and change events — does Redwood expose admin change history, API key deletion, token rotations?
[08:36] Maya: yes admin audit events include user role changes, API key creation/deletion, model deploys, configuration changes. those events can be pushed to your SIEM or exported to your bucket. retention and field-level details are configurable for enterprise.
[08:51] Priya: how granular are the logs — do you include request/response content in logs?
[08:56] Alex: by default we log metadata and request/response hashes; we do not persist full customer prompt/response content in standard audit logs unless you opt into that for debugging. if you need content-level logging for internal compliance we support customer-managed content sinks with encryption.
[09:13] Liam: that is important — we can't have prompts escaping our region nor stored in Redwood-managed buckets without CMK.
[09:20] Maya: yes we can route content to your bucket encrypted with your KMS. that requires a pilot and network setup.
[09:27] Tom: question on long term certs — you mentioned HSM signing for logs, is that supported for hosted customers?
[09:34] Maya: yes, we maintain an HSM for signing but for the strongest guarantees we recommend customer HSM or KMS with key wrap; we can provide signed manifests and hashes.
[09:44] Alex: any regulatory vertical concerns like FDA for manufacturing traces?
[09:48] Priya: our customers include regulated manufacturers; internal audit will focus on change control and traceability.
[09:54] Maya: we'll include an evidence package for change control processes and deploy logs for the pilot.
[10:00] Dana: procurement will ask for cyber insurance and SLA entitlements, can you share carrier info?
[10:06] Alex: yes, we can share our insurance summary in the Trust Center.
[10:10] Tom: any blockers for us to get trial access to Trust Center?
[10:14] Alex: we can provision read-only access once NDA reviewed — simplest route is we share SOC 2 and the control matrix first so legal can triage.
[10:22] Priya: can you show a short demo of where the trust center lives in the console? we just want to see how artifacts are surfaced.
[10:29] Maya: sure, i can do a quick screen share next call. for today i can describe: the Trust Center has a documents tab, a controls mapping page, and a report access admin where you invite external auditors to view sanitized reports.
[10:46] Alex: okay i want to call out one common confusion — model caching/kv cache retention. auditors sometimes think the KV cache holds customer prompts long term; actually KV is ephemeral per session and can be disabled. we'll add a note in the control mapping about KV cache lifecycle.
[11:05] Tom: perfect. any notes on model explainability requirements?
[11:09] Maya: we capture model version, prompt templates, and deterministic seeds in logs for reproducibility. for full explainability we recommend saved eval datasets in your bucket.
[11:22] Alex: wrapping up, let's recap the concrete items and owners.
[11:27] Alex: Action — Alex to share SOC 2 Type II and subprocessor list; Maya to send pilot plan; Tom to send control checklist; Liam to confirm network rules.
[11:39] Tom: sounds good. can we aim for a pilot kickoff week of Nov 17th? that's our preferred date.
[11:46] Dana: legal will try to clear SOC 2 by Nov 11th.
[11:50] Alex: we'll be ready to support and set up a technical kickoff once we have access. thanks everyone.
[11:58] Maya: one more thing — for the pilot we'll need an engineer-level contact from you for setup, can Liam be that?
[12:04] Liam: yes, that's me.
[12:06] Alex: great. i'll follow up with calendar invite for pilot kickoff and upload the docs. thanks all.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional word swaps (e.g., "Red would" for Redwood), some acronyms expanded incorrectly (e.g., SCIM transcribed as 'skim'). The transcript was lightly edited for legibility but retains filler words and pauses.

Attachments referenced: Trust Center link (to be provided), SOC2 Type II PDF (to be uploaded), Control matrix CSV (mapping to ISO Annex A), Pilot test plan draft (Maya to send).
